items.difficulty_reason: The lemma compares two topologies on M = lim H^p(C, F_n): the limit topology and the I-adic topology, showing they agree under an ascending chain condition on the graded module of the H^p(C, I^n F_{n+1}) (statement lines 4864-4880). The proof has three genuinely different ingredients: the containment I^n M contained in F^n giving one inclusion of topologies, the graded finite generation produced by the chain condition which supplies elements a_i that control F^n/F^{n+1} (proof lines 4890-4911), and the passage from density of IF^n in F^{n+1} to equality via the open mapping lemma applied to the map u : (F^n)^{direct sum r} -> F^{n+1} built from generators of I (proof lines 4914-4937). The claim is H2: a multi-step topological argument whose hardest step is the open mapping application.
